# Funnel

**Status:** specced, not built.
**Article:** [Finding Your Next Job, with AI](/aging-well/next-job.md) — "keep the search alive."
**Precedent:** [`budget-from-statements`](/aging-well/budget-from-statements.md) — a browser tab, your own files, nothing uploaded.

## What it does

Reads a CSV the reader keeps by hand (or exports from their `applications/`
folder — one row per subfolder), and turns it into the numbers the article's
weekly review asks for:

- Response, interview and offer rates, overall and broken down by source
  (board vs. referral vs. direct) and by which résumé version was sent.
- The same rates tagged by *which steps used AI* — evaluation, résumé, note,
  rehearsal — so a reader can see whether any of it actually moved their own
  funnel, not a survey's.
- Benchmarks alongside the reader's own numbers for calibration: about 3% of
  applicants get an interview and roughly 1 hire per 180 applicants
  (CareerPlug, 10M applications — see the
  [landscape research](/aging-well/research/landscape.md#4-evidence-on-what-works)),
  so a reader isn't grading themselves against nothing.

## Design constraint

This is the simplest of the three tools by a wide margin — it's arithmetic
over a CSV, not a model call — which is exactly why the article leads with
"measure" as something anyone with a spreadsheet can already do, and this
tool as a nicer way to see it, not a prerequisite for doing it.

## Open

- CSV schema: date, company, source, résumé version, AI-tag(s), stage
  reached, date of last movement — needs to match what a reader would
  actually keep, not what's easiest to compute from.
- Whether this belongs as its own page, or as a small embedded view inside
  the parse-and-gap tool once that exists.
